question: When the MUTCD requires an implementation decision, who must make that decision and what decision basis must be used?
model_answer: Direct Answer: When the MUTCD requires a decision for implementation, it must be made by an engineer, or by an individual under the supervision of an engineer, who has the appropriate experience and expertise. The decision must be based on engineering judgment or an engineering study, whichever the specific MUTCD provision requires. Supporting text clarifies that while the engineer develops the engineering-based solution, the final decision to implement it rests with the agency having jurisdiction over the roadway, based on the engineer's advice. Standards (mandatory): - "Where the content of this Manual requires a decision for implementation, such decisions shall be made by an engineer, or an individual under the supervision of an engineer, who has the appropriate levels of experience and expertise to make the traffic control device decision." - "Those decisions shall be made using engineering judgment or engineering study, as required by the MUTCD provision." Citations: - Section 1A.04 Standard §2 (p.2) - Section 1D.03 Support §4 (p.32) - Section 1A.01 Support §6 (p.1) - Section 1A.04 Support §1 (p.2)
gold_answer: The decision must be made by an engineer, or by an individual under the supervision of an engineer, who has the appropriate experience and expertise. The decision must use engineering judgment or an engineering study as required by the applicable MUTCD provision.
